13K likes, 156 comments - natgeo on October 20, 2026: "Some of the best reasons to travel in 2027 are far from the usual destinations. 🌎

National Geographic’s picks for Best of the World 2027 are here and features 25 destinations across six continents. 

Whether you're drawn to places steeped in history or the thrill of exploring the wild, there's no shortage of experiences worth planning a trip around. 

Find your next adventure and see our full #BestOfTheWorld 2027 guide at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Thomas Ekström".

22K likes, 109 comments - natgeo on October 13, 2026: "Presented by National Geographic Society in partnership with @Rolex. In the face of a changing world, these explorers are not giving up hope for our seas. Narrated by @auliicravalho, set sail across all five ocean basins in Expedition: Saving Our Seas, premiering Friday, November 13 at 9/8c on @natgeotv. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Rolex and The National Geographic Society are partnering on science-based expeditions to explore, study, and document change in the planet’s unique regions. #PerpetualPlanet.".

21K likes, 67 comments - natgeo on October 21, 2026: "Presented by @Rolex. These flamingos aren’t dancing—they’re “farming,” and their success depends on an unexpected ally: millions of fiddler crabs.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.".

174K likes, 206 comments - natgeo on October 19, 2026: "Photographing a big cat in the wild can take months of planning, with no guarantee of getting the shot. National Geographic photographer @stevewinterphoto has spent decades finding ways to capture these elusive animals, often using camera traps and working with people who know their habitats. 

Head to the link in bio to learn more about the efforts to protect them.".

79K likes, 871 comments - natgeo on October 20, 2026: "Don't let its stubby arms fool you—Koleken inakayali was an ambush predator from the abelisaurid family that once thrived in the Southern Hemisphere. Named by National Geographic Explorer @poldiego and colleagues, Koleken inakayali's tiny forelimbs continue to puzzle experts. 

Learn more about Koleken inakayali at the link in bio.".

187K likes, 362 comments - natgeo on October 19, 2026: "Presented by @Rolex. In the forests of East and Central Africa, the population of endangered mountain gorillas has nearly doubled since the 1990s, but diseases transmitted by humans remain a serious threat to their survival. Hoping to reduce this risk, National Geographic Explorer Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka is working with communities near Uganda’s Bwindi Impenetrable National Park to improve healthcare and hygiene.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Learn more at the link in bio.

Photographs by @hammond_robin".
